sentences.zh: 曹志

translations.literal: Cao Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi

sentences.zh: 曹志，字允恭，譙國譙人，魏陳思王植之孽子也。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi, courtesy name Yunggong, was a man of Qiao in the Principality of Qiao, and the bastard son of Cao Zhi, Prince of Chensi of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi, courtesy name Yunggong, came from Qiao in Qiao commandery. He was a younger son of Cao Zhi, the Wei prince known as the Prince of Chensi.

sentences.zh: 少好學，以才行稱，夷簡有大度，兼善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; he was praised for talent and conduct; he was calm and simple and had large capacity; he was also skilled at riding and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved study and won praise for ability and character—open and even-tempered, broad-minded, and adept both on horseback and with the bow.

sentences.zh: 植曰：「此保家主也。

translations.literal: Zhi said, "This one is a lord who will preserve the family."
translations.idiomatic: His father Cao Zhi said: "This boy will be the one to safeguard our house."

sentences.zh: 」立以為嗣。

translations.literal: " He established him as heir.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore named heir.

sentences.zh: 後改封濟北王。

translations.literal: Later his fief was changed and he was invested as Prince of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Later his title was changed to Prince of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 武帝為撫軍將軍，迎陳留王於鄴，志夜謁見，帝與語，自暮達旦，甚奇之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was General Who Upholds the Army and welcomed the Prince of Chenliu at Ye, Zhi visited him by night to present himself; the emperor conversed with him from dusk until dawn and greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wu still held the post of General Who Upholds the Army and had gone to Ye to welcome the Prince of Chenliu, Cao Zhi sought a nighttime audience. The two talked from dusk until dawn, and the emperor was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，降為鄄城縣公。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication, he was reduced to Duke of Juancheng county.
translations.idiomatic: After the abdication he was demoted to Duke of Juancheng county.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔在前世，雖曆運迭興，至於先代苗裔，傳祚不替，或列籓九服，式序王官。

translations.literal: An edict said, "In former ages, although dynastic fortunes rose and fell in turn, as for descendants of earlier houses, their succession was not cut off; some were arrayed as feudatories throughout the nine circuits, and orderly ranked at royal offices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "In ages past, though fate turned and dynasties rose and fell in succession, scions of earlier ruling houses often kept their lines unbroken—some held fiefs across the realm, others held titled posts at court.

sentences.zh: 選眾命賢，惟德是與，蓋至公之道也。

translations.literal: Choosing from the multitude and appointing the worthy, giving place only to virtue—this is the way of utmost impartiality."
translations.idiomatic: To elevate the worthy from among the many and grant office solely on grounds of virtue—that is the principle of perfect fairness."

sentences.zh: 魏氏諸王公養德藏器，壅滯曠久，前雖有詔，當須簡授，而自頃眾職少缺，未得式敘。

translations.literal: The various princes and dukes of the Wei house have nurtured virtue and concealed their talents; they have been blocked and stagnant for a long time. Although previously there was an edict that they should await selection for appointment, recently many offices have had few vacancies, and orderly advancement has not yet been achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei imperial princes have long kept their talents in reserve while blocked from advancement. Though an earlier edict promised they would be chosen for posts when appropriate, vacancies have lately been scarce and orderly promotions have still not gone forward.

sentences.zh: 前濟北王曹志履德清純，才高行潔，好古博物，為魏宗英，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The former Prince of Jibei, Cao Zhi, treads virtue pure and unsullied; his talent is high and his conduct spotless; he loves antiquity and broadly understands things; he is an outstanding man of the Wei imperial clan; I greatly commend him.
translations.idiomatic: The former Prince of Jibei, Cao Zhi, embodies unsullied virtue, combines rare talent with impeccable conduct, and delights in antiquity and wide learning—truly a distinguished member of the Wei house. I applaud him warmly.

sentences.zh: 其以志為樂平太守。

translations.literal: Let Zhi be made governor of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: Let Cao Zhi be appointed governor of Leping.

sentences.zh: 」志在郡上書，以為宜尊儒重道，請為博士置吏卒。

translations.literal: Closing the edict.] While Zhi was in the commandery he submitted a memorial, holding that Confucian learning and the Way should be honored; he requested that clerks and guards be assigned to the erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he memorialized the throne, arguing that Confucian scholarship and the moral Way deserved greater emphasis, and asking that each academic erudite be allotted clerks and attendants.

sentences.zh: 遷章武、趙郡太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be governor of Zhangwu and Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor successively at Zhangwu and Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 雖累郡職，不以政事為意，晝則遊獵，夜誦《詩》《書》，以聲色自娛，當時見者未能審其量也。

translations.literal: Although he accumulated successive commandery posts, he did not take administrative affairs to heart; by day he hunted, by night he recited the "Classic of Poetry" and the "Documents"; he amused himself with music and women; those who saw him at the time could not yet discern his measure.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served in several commanderies in succession, he showed little zeal for paperwork—hunting by day, reading the "Poetry" and "Documents" by night, and diverting himself with music and company—so contemporaries could not yet gauge his true depth.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，詔曰：「鄄城公曹志，篤行履素，達學通識，宜在儒林，以弘胄子之教。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianning era, an edict said, "The Duke of Juancheng, Cao Zhi, practices conduct earnest and plain; his learning is penetrating and his knowledge comprehensive; he should be placed among Confucian scholars to enlarge the instruction of imperial descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianning era an edict ran: "The Duke of Juancheng, Cao Zhi, leads an austere life of steadfast principle, with broad erudition and judgment. He belongs among classical scholars to strengthen the education of young nobles at school.

sentences.zh: 其以志為散騎常侍、國子博士。

translations.literal: Let Zhi be made Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary and Erudite of the Imperial Academy."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint him Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary and Erudite of the Imperial Academy."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘗閱《六代論》，問志曰：「是卿先王所作邪？

translations.literal: " The emperor once perused the "Treatise on the Six Ages" and asked Zhi, "Was this composed by your former prince?
translations.idiomatic: ": The emperor once read the "Treatise on the Six Ages" and asked Cao Zhi, "Did your late royal father write this?

sentences.zh: 」志對曰：「先王有手所作目錄，請歸尋按。

translations.literal: " Zhi replied, "The former prince had a handwritten catalogue of his compositions; allow me to return and search according to it.
translations.idiomatic: ": Cao Zhi answered, "My father kept a handwritten catalogue of his own works. Permit me to go home and check it.

sentences.zh: 」還奏曰：「按錄無此。

translations.literal: " He returned and memorialized, saying, "According to the catalogue, this is not among them.
translations.idiomatic: ": He reported back: "It does not appear on his list.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「誰作？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Who wrote it?
translations.idiomatic: ": "Then who wrote it?"

sentences.zh: 」志曰：「以臣所聞，是臣族父冏所作。

translations.literal: " Zhi said, "According to what I have heard, it was composed by my clansman uncle Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: ": "From what I have learned, my clansman Cao Jiong composed it.

sentences.zh: 以先王文高名著，欲令書傳於後，是以假託。

translations.literal: Because the former prince's literary fame was high and renowned, he wished to make the writing transmitted to later generations; therefore he falsely attributed it.
translations.idiomatic: Because my late father's literary reputation stood so high, he wanted the essay to survive under that name, so he lent him the authorship.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「古來亦多有是。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "From antiquity there have also been many cases of this.
translations.idiomatic: ": "Such borrowing of a famous name has plenty of precedent in history.

sentences.zh: 」顧謂公卿曰：「父子證明，足以為審。

translations.literal: " He turned and said to the dukes and ministers, "Father and son having testified, it is sufficient to be verified.
translations.idiomatic: ": Turning to the high ministers he added, "Father and son have both spoken—there is enough here to settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，可無復疑。」

translations.literal: From now onward, there need be no further doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter no one should doubt it again.

sentences.zh: 後遷祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Libationer of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸將之國，下太常議崇錫文物。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, You, was about to go to his state; an order was issued for the Minister of Ceremonies to deliberate honors and ritual gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince You of Qi was ordered to his princedom, the court instructed the Minister of Ceremonies to decide what honors and insignia should attend his departure.

sentences.zh: 時博士秦秀等以為齊王宜內匡朝政，不可之籓。

translations.literal: At that time the erudite Qin Xiu and others held that the Prince of Qi ought inwardly to rectify court governance and ought not go to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Qin Xiu and others argued that the prince ought to remain at court to steady the government rather than depart for his territorial seat.

sentences.zh: 志又常恨其父不得志于魏，因愴然歎曰：「安有如此之才，如此之親，不得樹本助化，而遠出海隅？

translations.literal: Zhi also constantly resented that his father had not realized his ambitions in Wei; therefore he sighed mournfully and said, "How can there be such talent and such closeness of kin, yet unable to plant roots and assist transformation, but instead sent far to a corner by the sea?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi still smarted over how his own father had been denied his due under Wei. He sighed in grief: "How can a man of such gifts and such royal kinship be barred from strengthening the dynasty at its core and sent instead to the rim of the empire?

sentences.zh: 晉朝之隆，其殆乎哉！

translations.literal: The flourishing of the Jin court—is it not endangered!
translations.idiomatic: If this is how Jin treats its own, what hope has the dynasty of ever prospering?

sentences.zh: 」乃奏議曰：「伏聞大司馬齊王當出籓東夏，備物盡禮，同之二伯。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he memorialized in deliberation, saying, "I have heard with reverence that the Grand Marshal, the Prince of Qi, is to go out to his fief in eastern Xia; full paraphernalia and complete ritual are to match the two elder lords.
translations.idiomatic: ": He therefore submitted a memorial: "I understand that the Prince of Qi, in his capacity as Grand Marshal, is being dispatched to his eastern princedom with every ritual honor due to the ancient archetypes of the two elder guardians of state.

sentences.zh: 今陛下為聖君，稷、契為賢臣，內有魯、衛之親，外有齊、晉之輔，坐而守安，此萬世之基也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is a sage lord; Ji and Xie are worthy ministers; within there is closeness like Lu and Wei; without there is aid like Qi and Jin; sitting and guarding tranquillity—this is the foundation for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is a sage ruler served by ministers worthy of Ji and Xie; within the palace you have the intimacy of Lu and Wei princes, beyond it the bulwark once provided by Qi and Jin. Secure the realm from the center and you lay the foundation for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 古之夾輔王室，同姓則周公其人也，異姓則太公其人也，皆身在內，五世反葬。

translations.literal: Of old those who flanked and aided the royal house—of the same surname it was the Duke of Zhou; of different surname it was the Grand Duke; both were personally within; for five generations they returned for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Those who propped up the house of Zhou—same-clan kin like the Duke of Zhou, affinal ministers like the Grand Duke Jiang—all remained at the capital, generation after generation, to be buried beside their kings.

sentences.zh: 後雖有五霸代興，桓、文譎主，下有請隧之僭，上有九錫之禮，終於譎而不正，驗於尾大不掉，豈與召公之歌《棠棣》，周詩之詠《鴟鴞》同日論哉！

translations.literal: Later although the Five Hegemons arose in succession, Huan and Wen were crafty lords; below there was the presumption of requesting tunnel burial; above there was the rite of the nine bestowals; in the end crafty and not upright, verified in the tail being large and not drooping—how can they be discussed on the same day as the Duke of Shao's song "Tangdi" and the Zhou poem's ode "Owl"!
translations.idiomatic: Later hegemons such as Huan of Qi and Wen of Jin ruled through guile; vassals pressed for kingly privileges while courts handed out the nine imperial gifts—power without legitimacy, the classic "tail too heavy to wag" problem. That record cannot stand beside the brotherly loyalty praised in the "Tangdi" ode or the warning woven through the "Owl".

sentences.zh: 今聖朝創業之始，始之不諒，後事難工。

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of the founding of the sage court, if the beginning is not sincere, later affairs are hard to bring to completion.
translations.idiomatic: This dynasty is still laying its first stones; begin without good faith and nothing built afterward will stand straight.

sentences.zh: 幹植不強，枝葉不茂；

translations.literal: If the trunk is not strong, branches and leaves are not lush;
translations.idiomatic: A weak trunk cannot sustain lush branches;

sentences.zh: 骨骾不存，皮膚不充。

translations.literal: if inner backbone does not remain, the outer skin is not filled out.
translations.idiomatic: strip away moral spine and the outward show collapses.

sentences.zh: 自羲皇以來，豈是一姓之獨有！

translations.literal: Since Fuxi the August, how could it be exclusively possessed by one surname!
translations.idiomatic: Since mythic antiquity no single lineage has ever monopolized Heaven's favor forever.

sentences.zh: 欲結其心者，當有磐石之固。

translations.literal: Those who wish to bind their hearts ought to have firmness like a great rock.
translations.idiomatic: Win men's loyalty only when your foundations stand like bedrock.

sentences.zh: 夫欲享萬世之利者，當與天下議之。

translations.literal: Those who wish to enjoy benefit for ten thousand generations ought to deliberate it with All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever would secure lasting advantage must weigh policy openly with the realm.

sentences.zh: 故天之聰明，自我人之聰明。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven's clarity and intelligence come from our people's clarity and intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven hears and sees through the hearing and sight of the people.

sentences.zh: 秦、魏欲獨擅其威，而財得沒其身；

translations.literal: Qin and Wei wished alone to monopolize their awesomeness, but in the end achieved only their bodies being submerged;
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Wei tried to hoard all authority and ended only by drowning themselves;

sentences.zh: 周、漢能分其利，而親疏為之用。

translations.literal: Zhou and Han were able to divide their benefit, and kinship close and distant thereby served them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Han shared power with kin and allies near and far, and those bonds served them well.

sentences.zh: 此自聖主之深慮，日月之所照。

translations.literal: This comes from the sage ruler's deep consideration; it is what sun and moon shine upon.
translations.idiomatic: Far-sighted rulers understood this; it is plain as sunlight.

sentences.zh: 事雖淺，當深謀之；

translations.literal: Although affairs may be shallow, one ought to plan them deeply;
translations.idiomatic: Even small matters deserve long forethought;

sentences.zh: 言雖輕，當重思之。

translations.literal: although words may be light, one ought to ponder them heavily.
translations.idiomatic: even casual words should be weighed with care.

sentences.zh: 志備位儒官，若言不及禮，是志寇竊。

translations.literal: Zhi occupies a place among Confucian officials; if my words do not reach ritual propriety, then Zhi is a bandit and thief.
translations.idiomatic: I hold a place among classical scholars: if my counsel falls short of ritual propriety, then I am nothing but a fraud occupying an office.

sentences.zh: 知忠不言，議所不敢。

translations.literal: To know loyalty and not speak—this is what I dare not in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: To see what loyalty requires and stay silent is what I dare not do in council.

sentences.zh: 志以為當如博士等議。

translations.literal: Zhi holds that it ought to be as the erudites and others have deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: I believe we should adopt the erudites' recommendation.

sentences.zh: 」議成當上，見其從弟高邑公嘉。

translations.literal: " When the deliberation was completed and was about to be submitted, he saw his younger male cousin, the Duke of Gaoyi, Jia.
translations.idiomatic: ": When the draft memorial was ready to go up, he showed it to his cousin Jia, Duke of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 嘉曰：「兄議甚切，百年之後必書晉史，目下將見責邪。

translations.literal: Jia said, "Elder's deliberation is very cutting; after a hundred years it will surely be written in Jin history—presently will you be blamed?
translations.idiomatic: Jia replied: "Brother, this argument cuts deep. Historians a century hence may praise you; those at court today may blame you instead.

sentences.zh: 」帝覽議，大怒曰：「曹志尚不明吾心，況四海乎！

translations.literal: " When the emperor read the deliberation, he was greatly angry and said, "Cao Zhi still does not understand my mind—how much less All-under-Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: ": The emperor read the memorial and flared with anger: "If even Cao Zhi cannot read my intent, what can I expect from the realm?

sentences.zh: 」以議者不指答所問，橫造異論，策免太常鄭默。

translations.literal: " Because the deliberators did not pointedly answer what was asked, but recklessly produced divergent opinions, by edict he dismissed Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mo.
translations.idiomatic: ": Deeming the authors evasive and argumentative rather than responsive, he cashiered Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mo by edict.

sentences.zh: 於是有司奏收志等結罪，詔惟免志官，以公還第，其餘皆付廷尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the relevant offices memorialized to seize Zhi and others for conspiracy crime; an edict merely dismissed Zhi from office and sent him as duke to his residence; the rest were all handed to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities then sought to arrest Cao Zhi and his allies on conspiracy charges; an edict stripped only Cao Zhi of office and allowed him to retire to his ducal mansion as commoner nobility, while the others were remanded to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 頃之，志復為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long, Zhi again became Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Cao Zhi was again appointed Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，居喪過禮，因此篤病，喜怒失常。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother; in occupying mourning he exceeded ritual; because of this he fell gravely ill, joy and anger losing normality.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's death plunged him into mourning so severe it exceeded prescribed rites; grief broke his health and unsettled his temper.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，太常奏以惡諡。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; the Minister of Ceremonies memorialized to give a bad posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of the era; the Minister of Ceremonies proposed a harsh posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 崔褒歎曰：「魏顆不從亂，以病為亂故也。

translations.literal: Cui Bao objected, saying, "Wei Ke would not follow a muddled order: he took his father's delirium, not the words themselves, as the true message."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bao protested: "Wei Ke defied a deranged command because he knew illness—not malice—had given it."

sentences.zh: 今諡曹志而諡其病，豈謂其病不為亂乎！

translations.literal: Now in assigning Zhi's posthumous name we fault his illness—does that mean we treat his illness as not disorder!
translations.idiomatic: If the court censures Cao Zhi for derangement in mourning, are we saying grief-induced illness counts as moral rebellion?

sentences.zh: 」於是諡為定。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the posthumous title was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: ": The court therefore settled on the posthumous name "Ding" (Steadfast).

sentences.zh: 庾峻

translations.literal: Yu Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun

sentences.zh: 庾峻，字山甫，潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Jun, courtesy name Shanfu, was a man of Yanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun, courtesy name Shanfu, came from Yanling in Yingchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖乘，才學洽聞，漢司徒辟，有道征，皆不就。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng had talent and learning broadly learned; the Han Minister of Education summoned him; he was summoned on account of moral conduct—he did not take office in any case.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu Cheng was widely read and accomplished; the Han court summoned him as Minister of Education and again as a candidate renowned for virtue—he declined every offer.

sentences.zh: 伯父嶷，中正簡素，仕魏為太僕。

translations.literal: His uncle Yi was impartial and upright, simple and plain; he served Wei as Minister Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yi served locally as regional merit evaluator, lived plainly, and rose under Wei to Minister Coachman.

sentences.zh: 父道，廉退貞固，養志不仕。

translations.literal: His father Dao was honest, retiring, chaste and firm; he nourished his aims and did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dao lived modestly and uprightly, devoted to study and never taking office.

sentences.zh: 牛馬有踶齧者，恐傷人，不貨於市。

translations.literal: If cattle or horses kicked or bit, fearing they would injure people, he did not sell them in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to sell at market any ox or horse known to kick or bite, lest it harm someone.

sentences.zh: 及諸子貴，賜拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: When his various sons became eminent, he was by imperial gift appointed Grand Palace Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Once his sons rose to honor, the court ennobled him as Grand Palace Grandee.

sentences.zh: 峻少好學，有才思。

translations.literal: Jun in youth loved learning and had talent and thought.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun loved scholarship from youth and showed literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 嘗游京師，聞魏散騎常侍蘇林老疾在家，往候之。

translations.literal: He once traveled to the capital; hearing that Wei Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary Su Lin was old and ill at home, he went to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: During a stay in the capital he learned that the veteran Wei scholar Su Lin lay ill at home and went to visit him.

sentences.zh: 林嘗就乘學，見峻流涕，良久曰：「尊祖高才而性退讓，慈和泛愛，清靜寡欲，不營當世，惟修德行而已。

translations.literal: Lin had once studied under Cheng; seeing Jun he wept and after a long time said, "Your honorable grandfather had high talent but a nature retiring and yielding; kindly and harmonious, broadly loving; pure and quiet, few desires; he did not scheme for the present age; he cultivated only virtue and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Su Lin had studied under Yu Cheng's household. Seeing Yu Jun he wept and finally said: "Your grandfather combined brilliance with humility—gentle, generous, detached from ambition and desire. He sought no office in his own day; he simply cultivated character.

sentences.zh: 鄢陵舊五六萬戶，聞今裁有數百。

translations.literal: Yanling formerly had fifty or sixty thousand households; I hear now there are only several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling once counted fifty or sixty thousand households; today rumors say only a few hundred remain.

sentences.zh: 君二父孩抱經亂，獨至今日，尊伯為當世令器，君兄弟復俊茂，此尊祖積德之所由也。」

translations.literal: Your two fathers were infants embracing through turmoil; alone they have reached today; your honorable uncle is a fine vessel of the present age; you brothers again are outstanding and lush—this is the reason of your honorable grandfather's accumulated virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Your fathers survived chaos as infants and lived to see better days; your uncle ranks among today's finest talents; you younger men shine as well—all this springs from the virtue your grandfather stored up."

sentences.zh: 曆郡功曹，舉計掾，州辟從事。

translations.literal: He passed through commandery merit clerk; was raised as accounting clerk; was summoned by the province as attendant clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He served as merit clerk in his commandery, rose as accounting clerk on recommendation, and entered provincial service as an attendant.

sentences.zh: 太常鄭袤見峻，大奇之，舉為博士。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mao saw Jun and greatly marveled at him; he raised him as erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mao thought him extraordinary and nominated him as an imperial erudite.

sentences.zh: 時重《莊》《老》而輕《經》《史》，駿懼雅道陵遲，乃潛心儒典。

translations.literal: At that time "Zhuangzi" and "Laozi" were esteemed while "Classics" and "Histories" were slighted; Jun feared the decline of the cultured Way; therefore he immersed his mind in Confucian canons.
translations.idiomatic: Fashion favored Zhuangzi and Laozi while slighting the Classics and histories; Yu Jun feared the erosion of serious learning and immersed himself in Confucian texts.

sentences.zh: 屬高貴鄉公幸太學，問《尚書》義于峻，峻援引師說，發明經旨，申暢疑滯，對答詳悉。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang visited the Imperial Academy and asked Yu Jun the meaning of the "Documents," Jun cited masters' explanations, illuminated the classic's intent, extended and clarified doubts and blockages; his answers were detailed and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Gaoguixiang toured the Imperial Academy and questioned him on the "Book of Documents," Yu Jun drew on established commentary, clarified knotty passages, and answered with meticulous thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Assistant Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 長安有大獄，久不決，拜峻侍御史，往斷之，朝野稱允。

translations.literal: Chang'an had a great prison case long unsettled; Jun was appointed attendant inspector and sent to decide it; court and countryside praised him as fitting.
translations.idiomatic: A major Chang'an lawsuit had stalled for years; Yu Jun received appointment as attendant inspector and settled it to universal acclaim.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，賜爵關中侯，遷司空長史，轉秘書監、御史中丞，拜侍中，加諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he was granted nobility as Marquis Within-the-Passes; he was promoted to chief clerk of the Minister of Works; transferred to Director of the Palace Library and palace clerk vice-director; appointed palace attendant; added Grand Counselor of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took the throne Yu Jun received the title Marquis Within-the-Passes, advanced to chief clerk of the Minister of Works, then Director of the Palace Library, vice-director of the imperial clerks, palace attendant, and concurrent Grand Counselor of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 常侍帝講《詩》，中庶子何劭論《風》《雅》正變之義，峻起難往反，四坐莫能屈之。

translations.literal: He constantly attended the emperor lecturing on the "Classic of Poetry"; attendant of the heir apparent He Shao discussed the meaning of orthodox and altered in "Airs" and "Elegantiae"; Jun rose to challenge back and forth; those seated on four sides none could bend him.
translations.idiomatic: When he attended the emperor's lectures on the "Classic of Poetry," He Shao, attendant to the heir, argued whether certain "Airs" and "Elegances" were canonical or decadent; Yu Jun rose to debate him round after round, and no one in the hall could best him.

sentences.zh: 是時風俗趣競，禮讓陵遲。

translations.literal: At this time custom tended to rivalry; ritual yielding declined.
translations.idiomatic: The age chased hollow rivalry while courtesy and modesty collapsed.

sentences.zh: 峻上疏曰：

translations.literal: Jun submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun therefore memorialized:

sentences.zh: 又疾世浮華，不修名實，著論以非之，文繁不載。

translations.literal: He also hated the world's superficial splendor and not cultivating name and substance; he composed a treatise to criticize it; the text was lengthy and is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise despised fashionable vanity and the neglect of genuine achievement, writing a lengthy critique not reproduced here.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，詔賜朝服一具、衣一襲、錢三十萬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; an edict gifted one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, and three hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of the era; an edict granted court robes, a burial garment, and three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 臨終，敕子瑉朝卒夕殯，幅巾布衣，葬勿擇日。

translations.literal: Facing death, he instructed his son Min: if he died in the morning, bury him that evening; wear only cloth headband and plain garments; select no lucky day for burial.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his son Yu Min to hold a same-day burial if he died before nightfall, to dress him only in plain cloth, and not to wait for an astrologically chosen burial day.

sentences.zh: 瑉奉遵遺命，斂以時服。

translations.literal: Min respectfully followed the dying command; he encoffined using timely dress.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Min obeyed, dressing the body for burial in everyday clothes as instructed.

sentences.zh: 二子：瑉、敳。

translations.literal: Two sons: Min and Ai.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Yu Min and Yu Ai.

translations.literal: A line break in the page layout marks the start of the subsection on the son.
translations.idiomatic: An editorial rule in the woodblock marks the turn to the subsection on his son.

sentences.zh: 子瑉

translations.literal: Son Min.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu Min

sentences.zh: =瑉字子琚。

translations.literal: The biography resumes under the same heading: Yu Min's courtesy name was Ziju.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Min's courtesy name was Ziju.

sentences.zh: 性淳和好學，行己忠恕。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and harmonious and he loved learning; in conducting himself he was loyal and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: He was mild, cordial, studious, and lived by loyalty and reciprocity.

sentences.zh: 少曆散騎常侍、本國中正、侍中，封長岑男。

translations.literal: In youth he passed through Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary, impartial upright of his native state, palace attendant; ennobled as Baron of Changcen.
translations.idiomatic: While young he served as Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary, regional merit evaluator for his home commandery, palace attendant, and Baron of Changcen.

sentences.zh: 懷帝之沒劉元海也，瑉從在平陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai fell into Liu Yuanhai's hands, Min followed and was at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huai fell captive to Liu Yuan (Liu Yuanhai), Yu Min accompanied him to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 元海大會，因使帝行酒，瑉不勝悲憤，再拜上酒，因大號哭，賊惡之。

translations.literal: Yuanhai held a great assembly; thereupon he made the emperor circulate wine; Min could not overcome grief and anger; twice bowing he presented wine; thereupon he loudly wept and wailed; the rebels hated him.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Liu Yuan ordered the Jin emperor to pour wine for his guests; Yu Min, overwhelmed with grief and rage, presented his cup with a double bow and burst into loud weeping—an affront his captors resented.

sentences.zh: 會有告瑉及王儁等謀應劉琨者，元海因圖弑逆，瑉等並遇害。

translations.literal: When there were those who reported Min and Wang Jun and others plotted to respond to Liu Kun, Yuanhai therefore plotted regicide; Min and others together met murder.
translations.idiomatic: When informants accused Yu Min, Wang Jun, and others of plotting to aid Liu Kun, Liu Yuan seized the excuse to stage a coup; Yu Min and the rest were killed.

sentences.zh: 初，洛陽之未陷也，瑉為侍中，直於省內，謂同僚許遐曰：「世路如此，禍難將及，吾當死乎此屋耳！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Luoyang had not yet fallen, Min was palace attendant, on duty inside the bureau; he said to colleague Xu Xia, "The world's roads are thus; disaster will arrive; I ought to die in this house!
translations.idiomatic: Before Luoyang fell, Yu Min was serving as palace attendant on duty in the palace offices. He told fellow attendant Xu Xia, "Affairs have come to this—calamity is near. I shall probably die inside these walls.

sentences.zh: 」及是，竟不免焉。

translations.literal: " When it came to this, in the end he did not escape.
translations.idiomatic: ": In the end his words proved true.

sentences.zh: 太元末，追諡曰貞。

translations.literal: At the end of Taiyuan, posthumously titled Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Taiyuan era the court posthumously titled him "Zhen" (Steadfast).

translations.literal: A ruled line in the edition separates the notice on the younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: The layout marks a break before the note on the younger brother.

sentences.zh: 瑉弟敳

translations.literal: Min's younger brother Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Min's younger brother, Yu Ai

sentences.zh: =敳字子嵩。

translations.literal: Ai's courtesy name was Zisong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai was styled Zisong.

sentences.zh: 長不滿七尺，而腰帶十圍，雅有遠韻。

translations.literal: His height did not reach seven chi, yet his belt spanned ten wei; he had refined remote resonance.
translations.idiomatic: Though barely seven chi tall, his girth measured ten hand-spans around the waist, and he carried an air of distant refinement.

sentences.zh: 為陳留相，未嘗以事嬰心，從容酣暢，寄通而已。

translations.literal: As chancellor of Chenliu he never let affairs cling to his mind; he was leisurely, drunk, and expansive—simply going along with the flow.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor of Chenliu he refused to let paperwork burden him—he lived at ease, drank freely, and drifted with circumstance.

sentences.zh: 處眾人中，居然獨立。

translations.literal: Placed among a crowd of people, he stood apart as if independent.
translations.idiomatic: In any gathering he seemed to stand utterly apart from the rest.

sentences.zh: 嘗讀《老》《莊》，曰：「正與人意暗同。

translations.literal: He once read the "Laozi" and "Zhuangzi" and said, "This truly agrees with what people feel in the dark."
translations.idiomatic: Reading the "Laozi" and "Zhuangzi" he remarked, "This speaks quietly to what I have always felt."

sentences.zh: 」太尉王衍雅重之。

translations.literal: " Grand Commandant Wang Yan greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Wang Yan held him in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 敳見王室多難，終知嬰禍，乃著《意賦》以豁情，猶賈誼之《服鳥》也。

translations.literal: Ai saw the royal house beset by many disasters and knew in the end he would encounter calamity; thereupon he composed the "Rhapsody on Intention" to open his feelings—like Jia Yi's "Fu on the Owl."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the house of Jin besieged by troubles, Yu Ai knew catastrophe would catch him in time; he wrote his "Rhapsody on Intention" to unburden his heart, in the spirit of Jia Yi's "Owl."

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：「至理歸於渾一兮，榮辱固亦同貫。

translations.literal: Its words said, "The utmost principle returns to undifferentiated oneness; glory and shame surely thread on one cord.
translations.idiomatic: It begins: "When the highest truth folds back into oneness, honor and disgrace run on the same string."

sentences.zh: 存亡既已均齊兮，正盡死復何歎。

translations.literal: Survival and loss already balanced alike—when right perishes in death, what again is there to sigh for?
translations.idiomatic: Life and death already balance out—why lament once your portion is spent?"

sentences.zh: 物咸定于無初兮，俟時至而後驗。

translations.literal: Things all settle in non-beginning; await the time's arrival and afterward verify.
translations.idiomatic: All things rest in that undivided origin and prove themselves only when their hour arrives."

sentences.zh: 若四節之素代兮，豈當今之得遠？

translations.literal: Like the four seasons' plain alternation—how could the present attain removal?
translations.idiomatic: They turn like the four seasons in steady succession—how could anyone escape that rhythm now?"

sentences.zh: 且安有壽之與夭兮，或者情橫多戀。

translations.literal: Moreover how could there be longevity versus early death—perhaps emotion crosses and multiplies attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Where is the difference between long life and short if craving skews every heart?"

sentences.zh: 宗統竟初不別兮，大德亡其情願。

translations.literal: Ancestral succession in the end does not distinguish at first; great virtue loses its emotional desires.
translations.idiomatic: Lineage begins undivided; the greatest virtue forgets private longing."

sentences.zh: 蠢動皆神之為兮，癡聖惟質所建。

translations.literal: Wriggling movement all is spirit's doing; foolish sagehood is only what substance establishes.
translations.idiomatic: Every twitch of life issues from spirit; blur saint and fool and you see only raw substance at work."

sentences.zh: 真人都遣穢累兮，性茫蕩而無岸。

translations.literal: Perfected persons all dispatch foul burdens; nature vast and boundless has no shore.
translations.idiomatic: The perfected shed every stain; nature stretches shoreless and wide."

sentences.zh: 縱驅於遼廓之庭兮，委體乎寂寥之館。

translations.literal: Though driven in the courtyard of vast expanse; entrust the body to the lodge of silence and emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: They roam the boundless court and yield their bodies to the silent inn."

sentences.zh: 天地短於朝生兮，億代促於始旦。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth are shorter than the creature born at dawn; hundred million ages are hurried in the first dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth shrink beside the mayfly; aeons vanish in a single morning."

sentences.zh: 顧瞻宇宙微細兮，眇若豪鋒之半。

translations.literal: Looking back on the universe minute and small—it is tiny like half a hair tip.
translations.idiomatic: The cosmos shrinks to half the tip of the finest hair."

sentences.zh: 飄搖玄曠之域兮，深漠暢而靡玩。

translations.literal: Fluttering in the dark vast domain; deep and silent, expansive, without play.
translations.idiomatic: You drift through dark immensity—deep, hollow, free, with nothing left to grasp."

sentences.zh: 兀與自然並體兮，融液忽而四散。

translations.literal: Stark with nature sharing substance; melting and dispersing suddenly in four directions.
translations.idiomatic: You stand dumb with the unnamed Dao, then melt away on every side."

sentences.zh: 」從子亮見賦，問曰：「若有意也，非賦所盡；

translations.literal: " His nephew Liang saw the rhapsody and asked, "If there is intention, it is not exhausted by the rhapsody;
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Yu Liang read the piece and asked: "If there is a point here, no poem can finish it;

sentences.zh: 若無意也，復何所賦？

translations.literal: if there is no intention, again what is there to rhapsodize?
translations.idiomatic: if there is none, why write a rhapsody at all?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「在有無之間耳！」

translations.literal: He answered, "Between being and non-being—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai answered: "Somewhere between yes and no—that is all."

sentences.zh: 遷吏部郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to section director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 是時天下多故，機變屢起，敳常靜默無為。

translations.literal: At that time All-under-Heaven had many incidents; stratagems and shifts arose repeatedly; Ai constantly was still, silent, and non-active.
translations.idiomatic: The realm seethed with intrigue, yet Yu Ai stayed quiet and took no initiative.

sentences.zh: 參東海王越太傅軍事，轉軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: He joined the Prince of Donghai, Yue's, Grand Tutor military staff; was transferred to Libationer-advisor of the army.
translations.idiomatic: He served on Prince Sima Yue of Donghai's staff as Grand Tutor's army adviser, then became army Libationer-delegate.

sentences.zh: 時越府多雋異，敳在其中，常自袖手。

translations.literal: At that time Yue's bureau had many outstanding and unusual men; Ai was among them, constantly keeping his own hands in his sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue's headquarters overflowed with talent, but Yu Ai usually stood back with folded arms.

sentences.zh: 豫州牧長史河南郭象善《老》《莊》，時人以為王弼之亞。

translations.literal: Chief clerk to the governor of Yuzhou, Guo Xiang of Henan, was good at the "Laozi" and "Zhuangzi"; people of the time considered him next after Wang Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang of Henan, chief clerk to the Yuzhou governor, excelled at the "Laozi" and "Zhuangzi"; contemporaries ranked him just below Wang Bi.

sentences.zh: 敳甚知之，每曰：「郭子玄何必減瘐子嵩」。

translations.literal: Ai greatly knew him; he constantly said, "Guo Zixuan why necessarily yield to Yu Zisong."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai admired him and often said, "Guo Zixuan need not take second place to Yu Zisong."

sentences.zh: 象後為太傅主簿，任事專勢。

translations.literal: Later Xiang became chief clerk to the Grand Tutor and in managing affairs monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guo Xiang became chief clerk to the Grand Tutor and wielded concentrated authority.

sentences.zh: 敳謂象曰：「卿自是當世大才，我疇昔之意都已盡矣。」

translations.literal: Ai said to Xiang, "Sir, you are yourself this age's great talent; my former intentions toward you are already exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai told him: "You are a giant of our age; whatever fond hopes I once nursed for you are spent."

sentences.zh: 敳有重名，為搢紳所推，而聚斂積實，談者譏之。

translations.literal: Ai had heavy renown, was pushed forward by the gentry belt-holders, but amassed and hoarded substantial wealth; talkers ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai enjoyed immense prestige among officialdom yet piled up private wealth, and wits mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 都官從事溫嶠奏之，敳更器嶠，目嶠森森如千丈松，雖礧砢多節，施之大廈，有棟樑之用。

translations.literal: Capital bureau attendant Wen Qiao memorialized against him; Ai further esteemed Qiao, viewing Qiao as towering like a thousand-foot pine—although rugged with many knots, applied to a great hall, he has ridgepole and beam use.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Qiao impeached him, Yu Ai only respected Wen more, calling him a towering pine—gnarled yet exactly the timber for a palace beam.

sentences.zh: 時劉輿見任于越，人士多為所構，惟敳縱心事外，無跡可間。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yu was employed by Yue; gentlemen mostly were framed by him—only Ai let his mind roam outside affairs; no trace could be exploited.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, trusted by Sima Yue, entrapped many officers, yet Yu Ai's aloofness left no opening.

sentences.zh: 後以其性儉家富，說越令就換錢千萬，冀其有吝，因此可乘。

translations.literal: Later because his nature was frugal yet his household rich, they persuaded Yue to order him to exchange cash of ten million, hoping he would be stingy—thereby an opening could be exploited.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his stinginess despite great wealth, Liu Yu urged Prince Yue to force Yu Ai to convert ten million cash, hoping meanness would give them leverage.

sentences.zh: 越于眾坐中問於敳，而敳乃穨然已醉，幘墮機上，以頭就穿取，徐答-{云}-：「下官家有二千萬，隨公所取矣。

translations.literal: Yue asked Ai among the seated assembly, but Ai was already collapsed drunk; his headcloth fell on the dais; he used his head to go through and fetch it; slowly answered saying, "This inferior official's household has twenty million; follow the duke's taking."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue pressed him in open court. Yu Ai was already slumped in drunkenness; his cap slipped onto the bench and he groped for it with his head before drawling, "I keep twenty million at home—take what you will."

sentences.zh: 」輿於是乃服。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yu submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu conceded defeat.

sentences.zh: 越甚悅，因曰：「不可以小人之慮度君子之心。

translations.literal: Yue was greatly pleased; thereupon said, "One cannot use petty men's considerations to measure gentlemen's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue was delighted and said: "Never gauge a gentleman with a petty man's suspicions.

sentences.zh: 」王衍不與敳交，敳卿之不置。

translations.literal: " Wang Yan did not associate with Ai; Ai "qing"d him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: ": Wang Yan refused his acquaintance, yet Yu Ai kept addressing him with the intimate "qing."

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「君不得為耳。

translations.literal: Yan said, "Sir cannot do it."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan said: "You may not use that form to me."

sentences.zh: 」敳曰：「卿自君我，我自卿卿。

translations.literal: " Ai said, "Sir, you yourself lord me; I myself qing-qing you.
translations.idiomatic: ": Yu Ai shot back: "You may call me 'lord' if you wish—I still call you 'dear."

sentences.zh: 我自用我家法，卿自用卿家法。

translations.literal: I myself use my household's law; sir yourself uses sir's household's law.
translations.idiomatic: I follow my family's manners; you follow yours."

sentences.zh: 」衍甚奇之。

translations.literal: " Yan greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was astonished—and impressed.

sentences.zh: 石勒之亂，與衍俱被害，時年五十。

translations.literal: At Shi Le's rebellion, together with Yan he was killed together; at the time his age was fifty.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le struck, Yu Ai died alongside Wang Yan; he was fifty.

sentences.zh: 郭象

translations.literal: Guo Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang

sentences.zh: 郭象，字子玄，少有才理，好《老》《莊》，能清言。

translations.literal: Guo Xiang, courtesy name Zixuan, in youth had talent in reasoning; he loved the "Laozi" and "Zhuangzi"; he could pure-talk.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang, courtesy name Zixuan, showed analytical gifts early, favored the "Laozi" and "Zhuangzi," and excelled at Pure Conversation.

sentences.zh: 太尉王衍每云：「聽象語，如懸河瀉水，注而不竭。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Yan constantly said, "Listening to Xiang's words is like a suspended river pouring water—it pours without exhausting.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Wang Yan used to say: "Listening to Guo Xiang is like watching a hanging river pour forth—it never runs dry."

sentences.zh: 」州郡辟召，不就。

translations.literal: " Provinces and commanderies summoned him; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Despite repeated provincial summons he never took office.

sentences.zh: 常閒居，以文論自娛。

translations.literal: He constantly dwelt idly, using literary essays to amuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement and amused himself with essays.

sentences.zh: 後辟司徒掾，稍至黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as steward of the Minister of Education; gradually reached Gentleman of the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually accepted appointment as a steward to the Minister of Education and rose to Gentleman of the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 東海王越引為太傅主簿，甚見親委，遂任職當權，熏灼內外，由是素論去之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Donghai, Yue, drew him in as chief clerk to the Grand Tutor; he was greatly seen as intimate and entrusted; thereupon holding office grasped power, scorching inside and outside; because of this pure opinion abandoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Yue of Donghai made him Grand Tutor's chief clerk and leaned on him heavily; Guo Xiang wielded real power and flaunted it at court and beyond, so opinion turned against him.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末病卒，著碑論十二篇。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia he died of illness; he composed twelve stele treatises.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness late in the Yongjia era, leaving twelve commemorative essays.

sentences.zh: 先是，注《莊子》者數十家，莫能究其旨統。

translations.literal: Earlier, those who annotated the "Zhuangzi" were several tens of houses; none could exhaust its aim's continuity.
translations.idiomatic: Before him dozens had annotated the "Zhuangzi," yet none had mastered its overarching design.

sentences.zh: 向秀於舊注外而為解義，妙演奇致，大暢玄風，惟《秋水》、《至樂》二篇未竟而秀卒。

translations.literal: Xiang Xiu beyond old annotations composed explanatory meanings; wonderfully extending marvelous reaches, greatly spreading dark wind—only the two chapters "Autumn Floods" and "Perfect Joy" were not finished and Xiu died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiu broke new ground beyond older glosses, unfolding subtleties that carried Dark Learning to new heights, but he died before finishing "Autumn Floods" and "Perfect Joy."

sentences.zh: 秀子幼，其義零落，然頗有別本遷流。

translations.literal: Xiu's son was young; its meanings scattered and fell; yet there were rather alternate copies circulating.
translations.idiomatic: His son was too young to preserve the work, and the commentary scattered, though stray copies still circulated.

sentences.zh: 象為人行薄，以秀義不傳於世，遂竊以為己注，乃自注《秋水》、《至樂》二篇，又易《馬蹄》一篇，其餘眾篇或點定文句而巳。

translations.literal: Xiang's conduct for people was thin; because Xiu's meanings were not transmitted in the world, he thereupon stole them and made them his own annotations; then himself annotated the two chapters "Autumn Floods" and "Perfect Joy"; also altered one chapter "Horse's Hoofs"; the remaining many chapters perhaps dotted and settled sentences only.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang, a man of shallow integrity, saw Xiang Xiu's insights unpublished and appropriated them as his own: he supplied the two unfinished scrolls, rewrote "Horse's Hoofs," and merely tweaked wording elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 其後秀義別本出，故今有向、郭二《莊》，其義一也。

translations.literal: Afterward Xiu's meanings' alternate copy emerged; therefore now there are two "Zhuangzi" of Xiang and Guo; their meanings are one.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Xiu's original resurfaced, both versions remained in circulation—the doctrine is one even if the names differ.

sentences.zh: 庾純

translations.literal: Yu Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun

sentences.zh: 庾純，字謀甫，博學有才義，為世儒宗。

translations.literal: Yu Chun, courtesy name Moufu, broadly learned had talent and righteousness; he was the age's Confucian patriarch.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun, courtesy name Moufu, was learned, principled, and revered as a Confucian leader of his day.

sentences.zh: 郡補主簿，仍參征南府，累遷黃門侍郎，封關內侯，曆中書令、河南尹。

translations.literal: The commandery supplemented him as chief clerk; still joined the south-conquering headquarters; accumulated promotions to Gentleman of the Yellow Gates; ennobled as marquis within the passes; passed through Palace Secretariat director, governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from commandery clerk and aide in the southern expedition headquarters to Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, Marquis Within-the-Passes, Palace Secretariat director, and governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 初，純以賈充奸佞，與任愷共舉充西鎮關中，充由是不平。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chun because Jia Chong was treacherous and flattering, together with Ren Kai jointly raised Chong to west garrison Guanzhong; Chong because of this was not level.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yu Chun had joined Ren Kai in urging that Jia Chong—crafty and sycophantic—be posted west to guard Guanzhong, which earned Jia's lasting resentment.

sentences.zh: 充嘗宴朝士，而純後至，充謂曰：「君行常居人前，今何以在後？

translations.literal: Chong once feasted court gentlemen, but Chun arrived late; Chong said to him, "Sir's conduct constantly resides before people—now why are you behind?
translations.idiomatic: At one court banquet Yu Chun arrived late. Jia Chong asked: "You usually push to the front—why lag today?"

sentences.zh: 」純曰：「旦有小市井事不了，是以來後。

translations.literal: " Chun said, "This morning there were small marketplace affairs not finished; therefore came late.
translations.idiomatic: ": "Minor market errands detained me this morning."

sentences.zh: 」世言純之先嘗有伍伯者，充之先有市魁者，充、純以此相譏焉。

translations.literal: " The world says Chun's ancestor once had a squad leader; Chong's ancestor had a market chief; Chong and Chun used this mutually to ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Gossip said Yu Chun's forebears had been market bailiffs and Jia Chong's family market bosses—the two traded barbs on that score.

sentences.zh: 充自以位隆望重，意殊不平。

translations.literal: Chong himself thought his position eminent and renown heavy; his intent was especially not level.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong, confident in his senior rank, nursed a deeper grudge.

sentences.zh: 及純行酒，充不時飲。

translations.literal: When Chun circulated wine, Chong did not drink in time.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chun poured the toasts, Jia Chong refused to drink on cue.

sentences.zh: 純曰：「長者為壽，何敢爾乎！

translations.literal: Chun said, "The elder performs the longevity toast—how dare thus!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun said: "An elder offers you a cup—how dare you refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」充曰：「父老不歸供養，將何言也！

translations.literal: " Chong said, "Father old does not return to supply nurture—what words will there be!
translations.idiomatic: ": Jia Chong sneered: "You refuse to go home and care for an aging father—what right have you to lecture me?"

sentences.zh: 」純因發怒曰：「賈充！

translations.literal: " Chun thereupon burst angry saying, "Jia Chong!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun exploded: "Jia Chong!

sentences.zh: 天下凶凶，由爾一人。

translations.literal: All-under-Heaven turbulent turbulent—from you one person.
translations.idiomatic: You alone have thrown the realm into chaos!"

sentences.zh: 」充曰：「充輔佐二世，蕩平巴、蜀，有何罪而天下為之凶凶？

translations.literal: " Chong said, "Chong aided two generations, swept pacified Ba and Shu—what crime and All-under-Heaven for it turbulent turbulent?
translations.idiomatic: ": Jia Chong retorted: "I served two reigns and crushed Ba and Shu—what crime turns the world against me?"

sentences.zh: 」純曰：「高貴鄉公何在？

translations.literal: " Chun said, "Where is the Duke of Gaoguixiang?
translations.idiomatic: ": "Then where is the Duke of Gaoguixiang?"

sentences.zh: 」眾坐因罷。

translations.literal: " The seated assembly thereupon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The banquet broke up on the spot.

sentences.zh: 充左右欲執純，中護軍羊琇、侍中王濟佑之，因得出。

translations.literal: Chong's left-right wished to seize Chun; Central Protector Yang Xiu and palace attendant Wang Ji shielded him; thereby obtained to exit.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong's guards moved to seize Yu Chun, but Central Protector Yang Xiu and palace attendant Wang Ji shielded him until he escaped.

sentences.zh: 充慚怒，上表解職。

translations.literal: Chong ashamed-angry, submitted memorial resigning office.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated and furious, Jia Chong memorialized his resignation.

sentences.zh: 純懼，上河南尹、關內侯印綬，上表自劾曰：

translations.literal: Chun feared; submitted Henan governor and marquis within the passes seals and ribbons; submitted memorial self-impeaching saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun, alarmed, returned his seals as governor of Henan and Marquis Within-the-Passes and impeached himself:

sentences.zh: 御史中丞孔恂劾純，請免官。

translations.literal: Palace clerk vice-director Kong Xun impeached Chun, requesting dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-director of the palace clerks Kong Xun impeached Yu Chun and asked that he be cashiered.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「先王崇尊卑之禮，明貴賤之序，著溫克之德，記沈酗之禍，所以光宣道化，示人軌儀也。

translations.literal: An edict said, "The former kings elevated high-low ritual; clarified noble-base order; wrote warm restraint virtue; recorded drowning-drunk disaster—thereby to brighten extend Way transformation, show people norm and model.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Ancient kings honored rank, distinguished noble from base, praised sober restraint, and warned against drunken excess—all to spread moral teaching and set an example.

sentences.zh: 昔廣漢陵慢宰相，獲犯上之刑；

translations.literal: Formerly Guanghan insulted-slowed the chancellor; obtained the punishment of offending superiors;
translations.idiomatic: Guanghan once insulted a chancellor and paid for lèse-majesté;

sentences.zh: 灌夫托醉肆忿，致誅斃之罪。

translations.literal: Guan Fu pretended drunk unleashed rage, caused execution-killing crime.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu feigned drunken rage and earned execution.

sentences.zh: 純以凡才，備位卿尹，不惟謙敬之節，不忌覆車之戒，陵上無禮，悖言自口，宜加顯黜，以肅朝倫。

translations.literal: Chun by ordinary talent occupies position minister governor; does not only humble-respect demeanor; does not fear overturned cart warning; offends superiors without ritual; perverse words from mouth—ought add manifest demotion, thereby to solemnize court relations.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun holds high office without special gifts, yet ignores humility, forgets the warnings of past scandal, insults his superiors, and lets reckless words fly—he should be dismissed outright to restore court discipline.

sentences.zh: 」遂免純官。

translations.literal: " Thereupon dismissed Chun from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun was therefore stripped of his posts.

sentences.zh: 又以純父老不求供養，使據禮典正其臧否。

translations.literal: Again because Chun's father was old and did not seek supply nurture, ordered according to ritual canons to rectify his good-bad.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered his filial record examined because he had left an aged father unattended.

sentences.zh: 太傅何曾、太尉荀顗、驃騎將軍齊王攸議曰：「凡斷正臧否，宜先稽之禮、律。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor He Ceng, Grand Commandant Xun Yi, Cavalry-in-Ordinary General Prince of Qi You deliberated saying, "Whenever judging rectifying good-bad, ought first examine ritual and statute.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor He Ceng, Grand Commandant Xun Yi, and Prince Sima You of Qi ruled: "Verdicts on conduct must rest on ritual and written law.

sentences.zh: 八十者，一子不從政；

translations.literal: For eighty-year-olds, one son does not follow office;
translations.idiomatic: At eighty a family may excuse one son from office;

sentences.zh: 九十者，其家不從政。

translations.literal: for ninety-year-olds, their household does not follow office.
translations.idiomatic: at ninety the entire household may stand aside.

sentences.zh: 新令亦如之。

translations.literal: The new order likewise is thus.
translations.idiomatic: The current statute says the same.

sentences.zh: 按純父年八十一，兄弟六人，三人在家，不廢侍養。

translations.literal: Investigate: Chun's father's age eighty-one; brothers six persons; three persons at home; not abandoned attendant nurture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun's father was eighty-one with six sons—three remained at home, so care never lapsed.

sentences.zh: 純不求供養，其於禮、律未有違也。

translations.literal: Chun not seeking supply nurture—as to ritual and statute there is no violation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun's absence therefore violated neither ritual nor statute.

sentences.zh: 司空公以純備位卿尹，望其有加於人。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works duke because Chun occupies position minister governor, hopes him to have excess over people.
translations.idiomatic: As minister-governor he was expected to model higher standards.

sentences.zh: 而純荒醉，肆其忿怒。

translations.literal: But Chun wasteland drunk, unleashes his angry rage.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he vented drunken rage.

sentences.zh: 臣以為純不遠布孝至之行，而近習常人之失，應在譏貶。

translations.literal: Your subject thinks Chun does not broadly spread utmost filial conduct, but near practices common men's faults—ought to be in ridicule-demotion.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that he failed to exemplify the loftiest filial devotion yet merely stumbled as ordinary men do—deserving censure, not harsh punishment.

sentences.zh: 」司徒石苞議：「純榮官忘親，惡聞格言，不忠不孝，宜除名削爵土。

translations.literal: " Minister of Education Shi Bao deliberated: "Chun glorious office forgot kin; hates hearing model words; not loyal not filial—ought remove name and shave noble territory.
translations.idiomatic: ": Minister of Education Shi Bao argued for erasing his name and stripping his fief for valuing office over family and spurning moral counsel.

sentences.zh: 」司徒西曹掾劉斌議以為：

translations.literal: " Minister of Education west bureau aide Liu Bin deliberated holding:
translations.idiomatic: ": The Minister of Education's aide Liu Bin replied:

sentences.zh: 河南功曹史龐劄等表曰：

translations.literal: Henan merit clerk clerk Pang Zha and others memorialized saying:
translations.idiomatic: Pang Zha and other Henan clerks memorialized:

sentences.zh: 帝復下詔曰：「自中世以來，多為貴重順意，賤者生情，故令釋之、定國得揚名於前世。

translations.literal: The emperor again issued edict saying, "Since middle ages many act for noble heavy convenient intent; base persons generate emotion—therefore made Shi and Dingguo obtain raising name in former age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded: "Since mid-Han times judges have favored the mighty and blamed the weak—yet Zhang Shi and Yu Dingguo won fame by doing otherwise.

sentences.zh: 今議責庾純，不惟溫克，醉酒沈湎，此責人以齊聖也。

translations.literal: Now deliberation blames Yu Chun, not only warm restraint; drunk wine drowning-drowned—this blames people by equal sagehood.
translations.idiomatic: Now you fault Yu Chun for drunkenness—yet demand of him the restraint of a sage-king.

sentences.zh: 疑賈公亦醉，若其不醉，終不於百客之中責以不去官供養也。

translations.literal: Suspect Duke Jia also drunk; if he not drunk, in the end would not among hundred guests blame by not leaving office to supply nurture.
translations.idiomatic: I suspect Duke Jia was drunk himself; sober, he would hardly before a hundred guests fault a man for not quitting office to nurse his father.

sentences.zh: 大晉依聖人典禮，制臣子出處之宜，若有八十，皆當歸養，亦不獨純也。

translations.literal: Great Jin according to sage men's canonical rituals regulates minister-sons' exiting-entering fitness; if there is eighty, all ought return to nurture—not singly Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin follows sage kings in fixing when officials may serve or stay home: anyone with a parent over eighty must retire to care for them—not Yu Chun alone.

sentences.zh: 古人云：'由醉之言，俾出童羖。

translations.literal: Ancient men said: 'From drunk speech, make exit black ram.
translations.idiomatic: The classic warns that drink loosens the tongue—"they'll make you send out the black ram"—

sentences.zh: '明不責醉，恐失度也。

translations.literal: 'Bright does not blame drunk—fears losing measure.
translations.idiomatic: meaning one must not judge harsh words spoken in sobriety's absence for fear of upsetting measure."

sentences.zh: 所以免純者，當為將來之醉戒耳。

translations.literal: The reason for exempting Chun ought to be as warning for future drunkenness only.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun was spared chiefly to establish a precedent about drunken quarrels, not his filial record.

sentences.zh: 齊王、劉掾議當矣。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi and Clerk Liu's deliberation is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi and aide Liu Bin had the better reading.

sentences.zh: 」復以純為國子祭酒，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: " Again made Chun Libationer of the Imperial Academy; added Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun was restored as Libationer of the Imperial Academy with concurrent appointment as Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 後將軍荀眅于朝會中奏純以前坐不孝免黜，不宜升進。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the Rear Xun Min at court assembly memorialized Chun because previously sitting unfilial dismissed demoted—not ought promote advance.
translations.idiomatic: At court General Who Guards the Rear Xun Min attacked Yu Chun: having once been cashiered for alleged unfilial conduct, he should not be promoted.

sentences.zh: 侍中甄德進曰：「孝以顯親為大，祿養為榮。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Zhen De advanced saying, "Filiality takes glorifying kin as great; salary nurture as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Zhen De replied: "Filial piety shines when sons honor parents; stipends exist to support them.

sentences.zh: 詔赦純前愆，擢為近侍，兼掌教官，此純召不俟駕之日。

translations.literal: Edict pardoned Chun's former fault; raised him as close attendant; concurrently managed instructing officials—this is Chun's summon not await carriage day.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had already pardoned Yu Chun and raised him to palace service and academic office—the crisis when he did not wait for the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 而後將軍眅敢以私議貶奪公論，抗言矯情，誣罔朝廷，宜加貶黜。

translations.literal: Yet General Who Guards the Rear Min dares by private deliberation demote seize public verdict; resist speech fake emotion—deceive court—ought add demotion dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet General Xun Min now seeks to overturn consensus from private spite—defying the court with lies—and deserves demotion himself.

sentences.zh: 」眅坐免官。

translations.literal: " Min by sitting lost office.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Min was stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 初，眅與純俱為大將軍所辟，眅整麗車服，純率素而已，眅以為愧恨。

translations.literal: Earlier, Min and Chun together were summoned by the Grand General; Min neat beautified carriage and robes; Chun led plain only—Min took it as shame-hate.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago both men joined the Grand General's staff: Xun Min dressed his carriage and robes to the height of fashion while Yu Chun stayed plain—something Xun never forgave.

sentences.zh: 至是，毀純。

translations.literal: Coming to this, slandered Chun.
translations.idiomatic: That bitterness surfaced now in his slander.

sentences.zh: 眅既免黜，純更以此愧之，亟往慰勉之，時人稱純通恕。

translations.literal: Min already dismissed demoted, Chun further by this shamed him; urgently went to console encourage him—people of the time praised Chun's thorough forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun Min fell, Yu Chun visited him repeatedly to console him; contemporaries praised his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，以父憂去官。

translations.literal: Transferred to palace attendant; because father mourning left office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace attendant but resigned to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 起為御史中丞，轉尚書。

translations.literal: Raised as palace clerk vice-director; transferred to secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as vice-director of the palace clerks, he moved on to secretary in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 除魏郡太守，不之官，拜少府。

translations.literal: Appointed governor of Wei commandery; did not go to office; appointed Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Named governor of Wei commandery, he never took up the post and was instead appointed Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 年六十四卒。

translations.literal: Age sixty-four died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 子旉。

translations.literal: Son Fen.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yu Fen.

translations.literal: The edition inserts a ruled line before the subsection on the son.
translations.idiomatic: The layout marks the transition to his son's biography.

sentences.zh: 子旉

translations.literal: Son Fen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu Fen

sentences.zh: =旉字允臧。

translations.literal: Fen's courtesy name was Yuncang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fen's courtesy name was Yuncang.

sentences.zh: 少有清節，歷位博士。

translations.literal: In youth had pure integrity; passed through positions erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for integrity from youth, he rose through posts as an imperial erudite.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸之就國也，下禮官議崇錫之物。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi You went to his state, issued order for ritual officials to deliberate honors and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima You of Qi departed for his princedom, the court ordered ritual officers to decide appropriate insignia.

sentences.zh: 旉與博士太叔廣、劉暾、繆蔚、郭頤、秦秀、傅珍等上表諫曰：

translations.literal: Fen together with erudites Dashu Guang, Liu Tun, Mou Wei, Guo Yi, Qin Xiu, Fu Zhen and others submitted memorial remonstrating saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fen joined erudites Dashu Guang, Liu Tun, Mou Wei, Guo Yi, Qin Xiu, and Fu Zhen in memorializing against the plan:

sentences.zh: 旉草議，先以呈父純，純不禁。

translations.literal: Fen drafted deliberation; first used to present father Chun; Chun did not forbid.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fen drafted the protest and showed it first to his father; Yu Chun raised no objection.

sentences.zh: 太常鄭默、博士祭酒曹志並過其事。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mo and Libationer-erudite Cao Zhi together passed-examined the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zheng Mo and Libationer Cao Zhi added their endorsements.

sentences.zh: 武帝以博士不答所問，答所不問，大怒，事下有司。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu because erudites did not answer what was asked, answered what was not asked—greatly angry—matter sent to relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu raged that the scholars had dodged the question and debated irrelevancies; he handed the case to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 尚書硃整、褚䂮等奏：「旉等侵官離局，迷罔朝廷，崇飾惡言，假託無諱，請收旉等八人付廷尉科罪。

translations.literal: Secretaries Zhu Zheng, Chu Lü and others memorialized: "Fen and others encroach office depart bureau—deceive court—elevate adorn evil speech—pretext without taboo—request seize Fen and others eight persons deliver Minister of Justice assign crime.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zheng and Chu Lü of the Masters of Writing impeached the eight scholars for overstepping jurisdiction, misleading the throne, and spreading reckless rhetoric, demanding they be handed to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 」旉父純詣廷尉自首：「旉以議草見示，愚淺聽之。

translations.literal: " Fen's father Chun went to Minister of Justice self-surrender: "Fen used deliberation draft show me—foolish shallow listened to it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun went to the Minister of Justice and confessed: "My son showed me his draft; I foolishly assented."

sentences.zh: 」詔免純罪。

translations.literal: " Edict exempted Chun's crime.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forgave Yu Chun.

sentences.zh: 廷尉劉頌又奏旉等大不敬，棄市論，求平議。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Liu Song again memorialized Fen and others great irreverence—market abandonment verdict—sought level deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Song pressed for the death penalty for irreverence and asked senior ministers to review.

sentences.zh: 尚書又奏請報聽廷尉行刑。

translations.literal: Secretaries again memorialized requesting reply hear Minister of Justice carry out punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing memorialized again to authorize execution.

sentences.zh: 尚書夏侯駿謂硃整曰：「國家乃欲誅諫臣！

translations.literal: Secretary Xiahou Jun said to Zhu Zheng, "The state actually desires execute remonstrating ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Jun told Zhu Zheng: "The court would execute men for remonstrating?

sentences.zh: 官立八座，正為此時，卿可共駁正之。

translations.literal: Officials established eight seats—exactly for this time—you can together refute rectify it.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Seats exist precisely for moments like this—you must overturn this verdict together."

sentences.zh: 」整不從，駿怒起，曰：「非所望也！

translations.literal: " Zheng did not follow; Jun angry rose, said, "Not what was hoped!
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zheng refused; Xiahou Jun rose in anger: "You disappoint every expectation!"

sentences.zh: 」乃獨為駁議。

translations.literal: " Thereupon alone composed refutation deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the sole dissent himself.

sentences.zh: 左僕射魏舒、右僕射下邳王晃等從駿議。

translations.literal: Left vice-director Wei Shu, right vice-director Prince of Xiapi Huang and others followed Jun's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice-director Wei Shu, right vice-director Prince Sima Huang of Xiapi, and others sided with Xiahou Jun.

translations.idiomatic: Past sixty he combined three excellencies, drew revenue from a great fief, bore tutor's honors, and wielded the Minister of Education's scales.

translations.idiomatic: Both sons wore gold-sable pins as minister-generals flanking the throne.

translations.literal: Compare to ancient men—burden deep load heavy—although whole household all die—still not match position.
translations.idiomatic: Against antiquity's standard he owed a crushing debt—had his whole clan perished, it would scarcely repay such rank.

translations.idiomatic: Instead he flaunted excess, grew notorious across the realm, abandoned the Way, yet kept extraordinary office.

translations.idiomatic: By classical standards he failed both as minister and as steadfast ally.

translations.literal: Defiles august age's beauty—breaks human relations' teaching—produces All-under-Heaven's ugliness—shows later life's arrogance—nothing greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: He stained the dynasty's good name, broke moral instruction, bred public scandal, and taught youth contempt—nothing could exceed it.

sentences.zh: 自近世以來，宰臣輔相，未有受垢辱之聲，被有司之劾，父子塵累而蒙恩貸若曾者也。

translations.idiomatic: No recent chief minister carried such scandal or impeachment yet received imperial indulgence like He Zeng and his sons.

translations.literal: Duke of Zhou mourned two Ji generations' decline—grieved great teaching's not proceeding—thereupon made posthumous titles to record their ends.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou lamented declining virtue and authored posthumous names to close each life with moral judgment.

sentences.zh: 曾參奉之，啟手歸全，易簀而沒，蓋明慎終，死而後已。

translations.literal: Zeng Shen upheld it—open hands return whole—exchange mat then die—covers bright careful end—death then afterward stop.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Shen embodied it—straightening his limbs on his deathbed and swapping his mat—proving reverence unto death.

sentences.zh: 齊之史氏，亂世陪臣耳，猶書君賊，累死不懲。

translations.literal: Qi's historiographers—disordered age attendant ministers ears—still wrote ruler thief—accumulate death not punish.
translations.idiomatic: Even Qi chroniclers in turmoil branded murderous lords—death alone did not lift blame.

sentences.zh: 況於皇代守典之官，敢畏強盛，而不盡禮。

translations.literal: How much more for august age guarding canons' offices—dare fear strong flourishing—and not exhaust ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Surely officers who guard the statutes of this dynasty cannot shrink from power and shirk full ritual.

sentences.zh: 管子有言：「禮義廉恥，是謂四維，四維不張，國乃滅亡。

translations.literal: Guanzi has saying: "Ritual, righteousness, integrity, shame—these are called four cords; four cords not stretched—state then perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong called ritual, duty, integrity, and shame the state's four cords—slack them and the realm collapses.

sentences.zh: 」宰相大臣，人之表儀，若生極其情，死又無貶，是則帝室無正刑也。

translations.literal: " Chancellor great ministers—people's model appearance—if living exhaust their feelings—death again without demotion—then imperial house lacks correct punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers model conduct for everyone; if they indulge every whim alive and escape moral verdict in death, the court has no justice.

translations.idiomatic: What could restrain proud nobles then?

translations.idiomatic: Where could the four cords still anchor?

translations.literal: Emperor Wu accepted treacherous flatterers' evil plots—embraced succession-end's distant consideration—thereupon lorded this green soil—became shepherd eastern fence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu listened to sycophants and brooded on securing his own succession, so he invested him with Qi and sent him east as a frontier prince.

sentences.zh: 遠邇驚嗟，朝野失望。

translations.literal: Far and near startled sigh—court and wilds disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far murmured in shock; court and countryside were dismayed.

translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi and his fellows absorbed Confucian teaching, walked the scholars' path, risked themselves unstintingly, and trembled for the state.

translations.literal: Therefore able resist speech phoenix palace gate—offend violate dragon scales—body although briefly bent—Way also great!
translations.idiomatic: Thus they could speak boldly at the gate of the palace and brush the imperial dragon—though their persons suffered briefly, the Way they upheld shone great.

translations.literal: Yu clan generation carries pure virtue—seen praised in age—Ru and Ying's many strange gentlemen—from this take this.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu clan bore unstained virtue for generations and won renown—the Ru–Ying region bred rare talents, and here they proved it.

sentences.zh: 謀甫素疾佞邪，而發因醉飽，投鼠忌器，豈易由言。

translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun always despised sycophancy yet erupted while drunk—like hunting rats beside sacred vessels, wise counsel comes hard.

translations.idiomatic: Theft of coin is theft—Guo Zixuan stole another's fame and claimed his virtue as his own; is that not robbery?

translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The Wei house leaned on him as its bulwark—famous as Prince of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 潁川多士，峻亦飛英。

translations.literal: Yingchuan many gentlemen—Jun also flies blossom.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan teemed with talents; Yu Jun too rose in splendor.

sentences.zh: 長岑徇義，祭酒遺榮。

translations.literal: Changcen followed righteousness—Libationer left glory.
translations.idiomatic: Baron of Changcen died for honor; the Libationer cast aside glory.

sentences.zh: 謀甫三爵，酗醟斯作。

translations.literal: Moufu three goblets—drunk confusion thereupon arises.
translations.idiomatic: Three cups undid Moufu—drunken brawling followed.

sentences.zh: 象既攘善，秀惟癉惡。

translations.literal: Xiang already seized good—Xiu only exhausts evil.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang stole credit for good; Qin Xiu punished evil relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 旉獻嘉謀，幾趨鼎鑊。

translations.literal: Fen presented fine counsel—almost hastened cauldron kettle.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fen offered worthy counsel and nearly landed in the execution cauldron.
